stack.name: Fan stack
stack.does: The cylinder the fan turns in, its top flared to recover the air's speed; the blades turn with a small clearance to its wall.

beams.name: Mechanical equipment support
beams.does: The beams across the stack that carry the gear drive.

gb_case.name: Gear case
gb_case.does: Holds the three shafts in their bearings and the oil they run in. Amarillo repairs the drive in a shop: it comes off the tower whole first.

gb_cover.name: Vertical cover
gb_cover.does: The gear case's top, located on two tapered pins: the upper bearing cups of the output and intermediate shafts sit in it.

gb_seal_carrier.name: Vertical seal carrier and upper seal plate
gb_seal_carrier.does: Hold the output shaft's seals and, with their shim pack, set the output bearings' preload; the seal plate shields them from above.
gb_seal_carrier.material: Cast iron, steel shims, nitrile seals

gb_int_cover.name: Upper intermediate bearing cover
gb_int_cover.does: Closes the intermediate shaft's upper bearing; its shim pack sets that shaft's end play.

gb_out_shaft.name: Output shaft
gb_out_shaft.does: The vertical shaft the fan's hub sits on, turning with it.

gb_helical.name: Helical gear
gb_helical.does: Keyed on the output shaft, driven by the intermediate shaft's helical pinion: the drive's second reduction.

gb_out_brg_lo.name: Lower output bearing cone
gb_out_brg_lo.does: The tapered roller bearing under the helical gear, in its cup in the gear case.

gb_out_brg_up.name: Upper output bearing cone
gb_out_brg_up.does: The tapered roller bearing at the output shaft's top, in its cup in the vertical cover: it carries the fan's thrust.

gb_int_shaft.name: Intermediate shaft
gb_int_shaft.does: A vertical helical pinion shaft beside the output shaft: its spiral bevel gear takes the drive from the input pinion, its pinion turns the helical gear.

gb_bevel.name: Spiral bevel gear
gb_bevel.does: Keyed on the intermediate shaft between its spacers, meshing with the input shaft's pinion: the first reduction and the turn through a right angle. It and the pinion are a lapped matched set.

gb_int_brg_up.name: Upper intermediate bearing cone
gb_int_brg_up.does: The intermediate shaft's upper tapered roller bearing.

gb_int_brg_lo.name: Lower intermediate bearing cone
gb_int_brg_lo.does: The intermediate shaft's lower tapered roller bearing.

gb_in_carrier.name: Horizontal shaft carrier
gb_in_carrier.does: Holds the input shaft's two bearing cups and fits in a register in the gear case's side, match-marked to it.

gb_oil_seal.name: Horizontal oil seal plate
gb_oil_seal.does: Holds the input shaft's oil seals on the carrier's outer face.

gb_in_shaft.name: Input shaft
gb_in_shaft.does: Driven by the drive shaft from the motor; carries the spiral bevel pinion at its inner end.

gb_pinion.name: Spiral bevel pinion
gb_pinion.does: Keyed on the input shaft's inner end, meshing with the spiral bevel gear.

gb_in_brg_in.name: Inner input bearing cone
gb_in_brg_in.does: The input shaft's tapered roller bearing next to the pinion.

gb_in_brg_out.name: Outer input bearing cone
gb_in_brg_out.does: The input shaft's tapered roller bearing at the carrier's outer end; its locknuts set the shaft's end play.

gb_low_covers.name: Lower bearing covers
gb_low_covers.does: Close the output and intermediate shafts' lower bearing bores under the gear case; the lower cups sit above them.

hub.name: Fan hub
hub.does: The hub spool on the output shaft (on a bushing and key) with its two hub plates, the blades clamped between them.
hub.material: Ductile iron spool, coated steel plates, aluminium blade clamps

blades.name: Fan blades
blades.does: Clamped by their necks in the hub at a set pitch angle, they push the air up out of the stack. Each is balanced on its own and can be changed alone.

seal_disc.name: Seal disc
seal_disc.does: Covers the hub so that warm air does not fall back down through it.

drive_shaft.name: Drive shaft
drive_shaft.does: Joins the motor to the gear drive's input shaft: a hub on each shaft, flex discs and a composite spacer tube between them.
drive_shaft.material: Carbon fibre composite tube, stainless steel hubs

guard.name: Drive shaft guard
guard.does: Covers the drive shaft where it turns outside the stack.

motor.name: Motor: stator and frame
motor.does: The fan's motor on the deck outside the stack, its feet on the deck: the stator in its finned frame, cooled from outside by its own fan (IC 411).
motor.material: Cast iron frame, laminated electrical steel core, copper winding

terminal_box.name: Terminal box
terminal_box.does: Where the supply cable lands on the winding's terminals U1, V1, W1; record the connections before it is opened.

end_shield_de.name: Drive-end shield
end_shield_de.does: Closes the frame at the drive end and holds the drive-end bearing in its housing; its bearing cap keeps the grease in.

end_shield_nde.name: Non-drive-end shield
end_shield_nde.does: Closes the frame at the fan end and holds the non-drive-end bearing in its housing.

fan.name: Motor's cooling fan
fan.does: On the shaft's non-drive end: blows air along the frame's fins whichever way the motor turns (straight radial blades). A fan fitted with interference is replaced, not reused.

fan_cowl.name: Fan cowl
fan_cowl.does: Guards the fan and guides its air over the fins.
fan_cowl.sealed_why: The grille is part of the fan cowl: they come off as one.

grille.name: Air intake grille
grille.does: Lets the cooling air in at the cowl's end; kept clear of dirt.

rotor.name: Rotor
rotor.does: The squirrel-cage rotor on its shaft: the stator's field drives it round. Drawn out of the stator's bore without touching the winding.
rotor.material: Laminated steel core, aluminium cage, steel shaft

bearing_de.name: Drive-end bearing
bearing_de.does: A rolling bearing on the shaft at the drive end, in the drive-end shield: it carries the load the coupling puts on the shaft.

bearing_nde.name: Non-drive-end bearing
bearing_nde.does: A rolling bearing on the shaft at the fan end, in the non-drive-end shield.

text: The fan stack stays on the tower's deck.
The support beams stay across the stack.
Set the gear case on its beams, its input opening towards the motor.
why: Amarillo repairs the drive in a shop: it comes off the tower whole, drained of its oil, and its side and upper inspection plates (not drawn) come off first.
needs: beams
The gear case stands on the beams: they are there first.
The beams stay.

text: Press the lower output and intermediate bearing cups into the case and fit the lower bearing covers under them.
why: Amarillo tips the case on its back to reach them, the input opening up.
needs: gb_case
The covers close the gear case's lower bores: the case is there first.
The case stays.

text: Offer the horizontal shaft carrier, with a gasket, to the case's side opening, its match marks on the case's.
why: In the shop the input shaft with its pinion and bearings is built into the carrier and the carrier goes in whole on two guide pins; the steps here fit each part in place.
needs: gb_case
The carrier goes into the gear case's side: the case is there first.
The case stays.

text: Put the input shaft into the carrier.
needs: gb_in_carrier
The shaft runs in the carrier: fit the carrier first.
Draw the input shaft out of the carrier before the carrier is moved.

text: Key and press the spiral bevel pinion onto the shaft's inner end, against the oil slinger plate.
why: Antigalling compound on everything pressed on a shaft.
needs: gb_in_shaft
The pinion goes on the input shaft: put the shaft in first.
Press the pinion off before the shaft comes out.

text: Press the inner bearing cone onto the shaft next to the pinion, never on its roller cage.
needs: gb_in_shaft
The cone goes on the input shaft: put the shaft in first.
Press the inner cone off before the shaft comes out.

text: Press the outer bearing cone on and set the shaft's end play with its two locknuts.
why: Amarillo leaves the play to be felt by lifting the carrier, then sets it with a dial indicator (§10).
needs: gb_in_shaft
The cone goes on the input shaft: put the shaft in first.
Take the outer cone off before the shaft comes out.

text: Lower the output shaft into the case, on a strong back with the intermediate shaft, onto its lower cup.
why: The two vertical shafts go in and out together on a strong back across both, so that their lower bearings and helical gears are not damaged.
needs: gb_low_covers
The shaft runs in the lower cup over its cover: fit them first.
Lift the output shaft out before the lower covers come off.
gb_in_carrier
Amarillo puts the input assembly in before the vertical shafts go down.
Lift the vertical shafts out before the horizontal carrier is pulled.

text: The helical gear is pressed on the output shaft against its shoulder, keyed.
why: In the shop the gear and both bearing cones are pressed on before the shaft goes in, and come off once it is out (in the steps here they are fitted and taken off in place).
needs: gb_out_shaft
The gear goes on the output shaft: put the shaft in first.
Press the gear off before the shaft is lifted out.

text: The lower output bearing cone goes under the helical gear with the output shaft spacer.
needs: gb_out_shaft
The cone goes on the output shaft: put the shaft in first.
Press the cone off before the shaft is lifted out.

text: Press the upper output bearing cone on against the shaft's shoulder.
needs: gb_out_shaft
The cone goes on the output shaft: put the shaft in first.
Press the cone off before the shaft is lifted out.

text: Lower the intermediate shaft in beside the output shaft, the timing marks on its bevel gear on the pinion's.
why: Its lower bearing cone must clear the input shaft's bearing retainer on the way.
needs: gb_low_covers
The shaft runs in its lower cup over its cover: fit them first.
Lift the intermediate shaft out before the lower covers come off.
gb_in_carrier
Amarillo puts the input assembly in before the vertical shafts go down.
Lift the vertical shafts out before the horizontal carrier is pulled.

text: The spiral bevel gear is keyed and pressed on between its spacers.
why: The gear and the pinion are a lapped matched set, never separated.
needs: gb_int_shaft
The gear goes on the intermediate shaft: put the shaft in first.
Press the gear off before the shaft is lifted out.

text: The lower intermediate bearing cone goes on below the below-gear spacer.
needs: gb_int_shaft
The cone goes on the intermediate shaft: put the shaft in first.
Press the cone off before the shaft is lifted out.

text: Press the upper intermediate bearing cone on above the above-gear spacer.
needs: gb_int_shaft
The cone goes on the intermediate shaft: put the shaft in first.
Press the cone off before the shaft is lifted out.

text: Seal the case's top flange and lower the vertical cover onto its two tapered pins; bolt it down and slide the upper cups onto the cones.
why: It comes off with a hoist on two eye bolts in the seal carrier's and the bearing cover's holes.
needs: gb_out_brg_up
The cover's cups close over the upper cones: fit them first.
Lift the vertical cover off before the output shaft's upper cone.
gb_int_brg_up
The cover's cups close over the upper cones: fit them first.
Lift the vertical cover off before the intermediate shaft's upper cone.
gb_out_shaft
The cover closes over the output shaft: lower it in first.
Lift the vertical cover off before the output shaft comes out.
gb_int_shaft
The cover closes over the intermediate shaft: lower it in first.
Lift the vertical cover off before the intermediate shaft comes out.

text: Fit the upper intermediate bearing cover with its shim pack, the end play set to 0 to 0.001 inch.
why: Never mix up the shim packs: each sets its own shaft.
needs: gb_cover
The bearing cover sits on the vertical cover: fit that first.
Take the bearing cover off, keeping its shims, before the vertical cover.

text: Fit the vertical seal carrier with its seals and shim pack, then the upper seal plate clear of it.
needs: gb_cover
The seal carrier sits on the vertical cover: fit that first.
Take the seal plate and the seal carrier off, keeping the shims, before the vertical cover.

text: Slide the horizontal oil seal plate with its seals over the input shaft, its keyway taped.
why: Amarillo takes it off before the vertical cover; its old seals are thrown away. Then the drive is filled with oil.
needs: gb_in_carrier
The seal plate sits on the carrier's outer face: fit the carrier first.
Take the oil seal plate off before the carrier is pulled.
gb_in_brg_out
The seal plate closes over the outer bearing: fit it first.
Take the oil seal plate off before the outer bearing.

text: Set the hub on the output shaft, its key in the keyway, and lock its bushing's cap screws.
why: Its mating faces clean and dry; a thrust retainer (optional) holds it down where the shaft has no shoulder. Hudson gives the installation order only: taking the fan apart is its reverse, not a maker's removal procedure.
needs: gb_out_shaft
The hub sits on the output shaft: the gear drive is there first.
Take the hub off before the gear drive comes apart.
gb_seal_carrier
The hub stands over the seal carrier: fit it first.
Lift the hub off before the seal carrier comes off.

text: Clamp each blade's neck in its clamp halves between the hub plates, its thick leading edge to the left seen from its tip.
why: Each blade is balanced on its own and can be changed alone. Hudson gives the installation order only: taking the fan apart is its reverse, not a maker's removal procedure.
needs: hub
The blades are clamped in the hub: set the hub on first.
Take the blades out before the hub.

text: Set each blade's pitch with a protractor near its tip, tighten its four clamp bolts, then check the track and the sweep blade by blade.
why: The pitch within 0.2 degrees of the design; the tips' levels marked on the stack within an inch. Hudson gives the installation order only: taking the fan apart is its reverse, not a maker's removal procedure.
needs: blades
The bolts clamp the blades: put them in first.
Loosen and take out the clamp bolts before a blade comes out.

text: Bolt the seal disc's two halves together and set it on the six studs of the top hub plate.
why: It keeps warm air from falling back down through the hub. Hudson gives the installation order only: taking the fan apart is its reverse, not a maker's removal procedure.
needs: clamp_bolts
The seal disc goes on last, over the clamped blades' roots.
Take the seal disc off before the blades' clamp bolts.

text: Fit the seal disc's six nuts and washers.
why: Hudson gives the installation order only: taking the fan apart is its reverse, not a maker's removal procedure.
needs: seal_disc
The nuts hold the seal disc: put it on first.
Take the six nuts off first.

text: The motor stands on the deck outside the stack, on its shims.
why: Its own parts come apart as the motor kind's do. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

text: Slide the rotor into the stator's bore from the drive end, its weight carried so that it never rests on the winding.
why: A rotor dragged against the winding damages its insulation. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: motor
The rotor goes into the stator's bore: set the stator down first.
Draw the rotor out before the stator is moved.

text: Fit the drive-end bearing on the shaft, heated, pressing on its inner ring only.
why: In the shop the bearings go on the shaft before the rotor goes in, and come off it once the rotor is out (in the steps here they are fitted and taken off in place). Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

text: Fit the non-drive-end bearing on the shaft the same way.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

text: Fit the non-drive-end shield over its bearing and into the frame, with its bearing cap.
why: Its spigot is entered square, without forcing, so that the bearing is not loaded. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: bearing_nde
The shield's housing closes over the non-drive-end bearing: fit the bearing first.
Take the non-drive-end shield off before its bearing.

text: Fit the drive-end shield over its bearing and into the frame, with its bearing cap.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: bearing_de
The shield's housing closes over the drive-end bearing: fit the bearing first.
Take the drive-end shield off before its bearing.
rotor
The drive-end shield closes the stator over the rotor: put the rotor in first.
Take the drive-end shield off before the rotor is drawn out.

text: Fit the four drive-end shield bolts and tighten them evenly; turn the shaft by hand: it must turn freely.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: end_shield_de
The bolts hold the drive-end shield: fit the shield first.
Take the four bolts out before the drive-end shield comes off.

text: Push the fan onto the shaft's non-drive end and lock it.
why: A fan fitted with interference is pulled with a puller, never knocked off, and replaced. Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: end_shield_nde
The fan sits behind the non-drive-end shield: fit the shield first.
Pull the fan off before the non-drive-end shield comes off.
rotor
The fan goes on the rotor's shaft: put the rotor in first.
Pull the fan off before the rotor is drawn out: it is wider than the stator's bore.

text: Put the fan cowl over the fan.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: fan
The cowl closes over the fan: fit the fan first.
Take the fan cowl off before the fan.

text: The grille comes with the fan cowl.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.

text: Fit the four cowl screws.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: fan_cowl
The screws hold the cowl: put the cowl on first.
Take the four cowl screws out before the cowl comes off.

text: Fit the terminal box and connect the supply as recorded before it was opened.
why: Order derived from how the motor is built, not from a manual: no public manual read gives a numbered dismantling sequence.
needs: motor
The terminal box sits on the stator's frame: set the stator down first.
Take the terminal box off before the stator is moved.

text: Fit a hub on the motor's shaft and one on the gear drive's input shaft, put the spacer tube between them, bolt the flex discs to its end flanges, then check the alignment.
why: Amarillo gives the installation steps; taking it off is their reverse. The motor and the gear drive are aligned to each other before it goes in.
needs: gb_oil_seal
The drive shaft's hub goes on the input shaft outside its oil seal plate: fit the plate first.
Take the drive shaft off before the oil seal plate.
rotor
The drive shaft's other hub sits on the motor's shaft: put the rotor in first.
Take the drive shaft off before the motor's rotor is drawn out.
motor
The drive shaft joins the motor to the gear drive: set the motor down first.
Take the drive shaft off before the motor is moved.

text: Fit the drive shaft's guard.
why: The drive shaft never turns without its guard.
needs: drive_shaft
The guard covers the drive shaft: fit the shaft first.
Take the guard off first.
